what_happened: Job 20261026-145955-s7e2 ("Route all records/ readers to the athena/records worktree") failed in planning, before any code was written. After round 3 of 3 the critic still said the plan needed revising. It judged most of the plan sound: the path is defined once in paths.rs, load_current forms are added to RecordSet::load and Records::load, xtask already depends on athena-data, and the real-git fixture with a negative control fails on the old code. One major finding remained: a live reader in gh.rs (land_pr, lines 2512-2513) loads Records at the live HEAD. The plan does not classify it, move it, list the file, or put it on the scan allow-list. Either the scan test fails on the real tree, or `athena land` stops finding jobs after the cutover. Two minor findings: the scan patterns should also catch fully qualified paths like `crate::store::Records::load(`, and the introspect.rs sites look like live directory walks that should move rather than be left to the producer. The event lists no unmet acceptance criteria and no failed checks. Nothing was delivered.
cause: A sweeping change ("all readers") is planned without an enumerated, evidence-backed list of call sites. Nothing makes the reading or plan find every caller of the loaders against the code before the critic runs. The critic is the first stage to open gh.rs, and it has only three rounds and keeps no partial plan, so a site found in the last round fails the job. The plan also leaves some sites (introspect) for the producer to decide. This is the second planning failure in a row on the same request: the retry did not carry forward the earlier critic findings in a form that forces them to be closed. The earlier finding was the site generator reading a different directory, and this one is land_pr. The scan test is meant to be the completeness check, but it was designed from memory and not run against the real tree, so its allow-list was wrong.
prevention: Require any plan that changes "all readers/callers" of something to include a call-site inventory produced by actually running the scan against the current tree. Each hit must be marked move, allow-listed or out of scope, with a reason and its file added to the deliverables, and none may be left to the producer. The scan patterns must cover qualified and aliased forms. The critic's first round must check this inventory against its own grep. A retry must receive the prior attempt's critic findings as items that have to be closed. With this in place, land_pr, the introspect sites and the site generator would all have been found before round 3.
proposed_request: Point every reader of records/ at the athena/records worktree. First run a scan of the current tree for all loaders of records (Records::load, RecordSet::load, and fully qualified or aliased forms such as crate::store::Records::load) and write down every hit. Classify each hit as moved to the worktree path or allow-listed with a reason. Known sites to cover: gh.rs land_pr (resolves a job at live HEAD, so it must move or `athena land` loses jobs after the cutover), the introspect.rs directory walks (move them to records_root), and the study site generator, which reads studies/firstmate-work-handling and is out of scope. Define the worktree path once in paths.rs beside repo_state_dir. Add load_current forms to RecordSet::load and Records::load, and keep a fallback for when the worktree is absent. Acceptance: (1) a real-git fixture whose HEAD has no records/ loads the records through the worktree, and the same test fails on the old code; (2) `athena land` finds the job's records after the cutover, shown by a test that calls land_pr; (3) a scan test over the real tree fails if any unlisted reader loads records at HEAD, and it covers qualified paths; (4) the scan test is run with the exact command given, and cargo fmt, clippy and test pass. Files: paths.rs, records.rs, store.rs, gh.rs, introspect.rs, walltime.rs, and the scan test and its allow-list.
